items.title: ii) Calculating Enthalpy Change of Reaction (ΔH°r) using Enthalpies of formation (ΔH°f)

source_refs.note: ii) Calculating Enthalpy Change of Reaction (ΔH°r) using Enthalpies of formation (ΔH°f): a main subheading of 6.8 Hess's law of heat summation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 127-128.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 6.4
blocks.problem:
Calculate the enthalpy change of reaction of
C₂H₄ + HCl → C₂H₅Cl
Using Hess cycle with the help of following combustion data.
ΔH°f of C₂H₄ = + 52.2 KJ mol⁻¹
ΔH°f of HCl = -92.3 KJ mol⁻¹
ΔH°f of C₂H₅Cl = -109 KJ mol⁻¹

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The data given are enthalpies of formation (ΔH°f), not combustion data: ΔH = ΔH°f(C₂H₅Cl) – [ΔH°f(C₂H₄) + ΔH°f(HCl)] = –109 – [+52.2 + (–92.3)] = –68.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

blocks.alt: Hess cycle: C2H4(g) + HCl(g) goes to C2H5Cl(g) (delta H). Below, a blue box with the elements 2C(s) + 2 1/2 H2(g) + 1/2 Cl2(g); arrows go up from it to C2H4 (+52.2), to HCl (-92.3) and to C2H5Cl (-109). Dotted blue lines lead from the box to C2H5Cl.
blocks.caption: Hess cycle of Sample Problem 6.4 (original drawing after the figure printed on p127 of the textbook).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed cycle of Sample Problem 6.4 leaves out the ‘+’ between 2C(s) and 2½ H₂(g) and prints Cl as ‘CI’; both are written correctly above.

blocks.prompt:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change for the formation of methane:
6C(s) + 3H₂(g) → C₆H₆(l), ΔHf° = ?
The standard enthalpies of combustion of C(s), H₂(g) and C₆H₆(l) are –394 kJ mol⁻¹, –286 kJ mol⁻¹ and –3267 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively.
blocks.explanation: ΔH°f = [6 × (−394) + 3 × (−286)] − (−3267) = −2364 − 858 + 3267 = +45 kJ mol⁻¹. So the formation of benzene is endothermic. (The equation is the formation of benzene, not methane; see the Book correction.)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The equation 6C(s) + 3H₂(g) → C₆H₆(l) is the formation of benzene, C₆H₆, not methane; the question asks for the standard enthalpy change of formation of benzene.
